2.Brief fact which are necessary for disposal of this appeal is as follows:-
On 23.08.2019, when the appellant was driving an auto bearing Reg. No.TN 66 U 9619 in east to west direction in Covai-Siruvani Road along with his passengers, at that time, a car bearing Reg. No.TN 37 DX 8615 driven by its driver insured with the second respondent insurance company, driven the car in a rash and negligent V.Vignesh vs M.Kalimuthu on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113753232/
1 manner, hit against the auto, due to which, the accident had happened and appellant sustained injuries, Thereby, the appellant/claimant has filed a claim Petition before the Labour Court claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- against the owner of the vehicle and its insurer.
3. Before the Commissioner, during trial, in order to prove the case, on the side of the appellant, two witnesses were examined viz., PW1 and PW2 and marked 20 documents viz., Exs.P1 to P20,
On the side of the respondent/Insurance company, no witness was examined and no document was m a r k e d .
T h e T r i b u n a l , c o n s i d e r i n g t h e p l e a d i n g s , o r a l a n d d o c u m e n t a r y https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 27/06/2025 06:17:09 pm ) evidence, allowed the petition in part and awarded a sum of Rs.6,83,500/- as compensation to the claimant.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant has filed this appeal before this Court for enhancement of the compensation.

4. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submitted that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle belonging to the first respondent insured with the second respondent herein and erred in awarding a meagre and inadequate compensation to the appellant.

Due to the accident, the appellant has suffered loss of vision in left eye and as per accident register,
the appellant has sustained LE globe rupture, which is grievous in nature and the Doctor has assessed 30% disability.
Without considering the entire fact, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15000/- which is very meager.
The Tribunal without any basis has awarded inadequate compensation in respect of other heads, which needs to be interfered with.
5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the second respondent/insurance company submitted that the Tribunal has awarded compensation to the Claimant, which is highly excessive.
Without any https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 27/06/2025 06:17:09 pm ) basis, Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- which is exorbitant.

Apart from that a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards loss of amenities and Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium was awarded and the same are too high.
Hence, this Court may dismiss the appeal.
6. This Court gave its careful consideration to the submissions advanced by the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the materials available on record.
7. The factum of the accident is not disputed by the parties and so also the liability.
Therefore, this Court is not entering into the said aspect.
The only grievance of the claimant is with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded.
8. On perusal of the award, it is seen that the appellant was aged about 26 years at that time of the accident.
The claimant was earning Rs.25,000/- per month at the time of the accident.
Due to the accident, the claimant has sustained injuries and he lost is vision in the left eye.
However, the medical board assessed the disability at 30%.
Hence, the Tribunal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 27/06/2025 06:17:09 pm ) awarded 2,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings and Rs.1,00,000 was awarded in respect of loss of amenities.
However, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5000/- per percent in respect of disability and awarded Rs.1,50,000/- (Rs.5000/- X 30%).

9. In the result, the civil miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
The award passed and liability fastened against the respondents by the Tribunal is confirmed.

The respondents are to deposit the compensation amount with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum, jointly or severally, from the date of petition till the date of realization, after deducting the amount if any already deposited within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the same on making proper application before the Tribunal.
No costs.
